Silent failures of automated remediation may also go unnoticed.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Menu > Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create Rule and select the Compartment; switch to the Cloud Guard reporting Region
3. In Conditions, add event types: com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdismissed, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemremediated
4. Under Actions, add Notifications and select the desired Topic
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Implement **event-driven alerts** for Cloud Guard problem lifecycle events and route them to trusted **notification channels** and your **SOC/SIEM**. Enforce **least privilege** on publish/subscribe, align rules with the **reporting region**, and use **severity-based filtering** to prioritize response within a **defense-in-depth** approach.

oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_group_change.title: Event rule monitoring IAM group changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_group_change.description: **OCI Events rules** monitor **IAM group lifecycle events** (`creategroup`, `updategroup`, `deletegroup`) and include **notification actions** to generate alerts when these changes occur.
oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_group_change.risk: Without alerts on **IAM group changes**, unauthorized privilege changes can persist unnoticed, enabling **privilege escalation** and broader access. This undermines **confidentiality** and **integrity**, and delays response to identity misuse.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and set Name
3. In Condition, select Event types and add:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.creategroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletegroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updategroup
4. In Actions, add Notifications and select an existing Topic
5. Click Create to save the rule
remediation.recommendationText: Create **Events rules** for IAM group `create`, `update`, and `delete` and route them to **Notifications** channels consumed by the SOC. Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rules/topics, forward events to a **SIEM**, and periodically test alert delivery.

oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_policy_chang.title: Event rule monitoring IAM policy changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_policy_chang.description: **OCI Events rules** configured to capture **IAM policy create, update, and delete** events (`com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy`, `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy`, `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy`) and include a **notification action**.
oraclecloud.events_rule_iam_policy_chang.risk: Without alerts on **IAM policy changes**, permissions can be altered unnoticed, enabling **privilege escalation**, unauthorized data access, and persistent footholds. Delayed visibility degrades **confidentiality** and **integrity** and slows incident response across compartments.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service
2. Click Create Rule and set Display Name (leave Enabled)
3. Under Conditions, choose Event Type, set Service Name to Identity and Access Management, and select:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy
4. Under Actions, select Action Type: Notifications, then choose the target Topic
5. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Create OCI Events rules for `...createpolicy`, `...updatepolicy`, and `...deletepolicy` with a **notification action** to trusted channels. Enforce **least privilege** on IAM and Events administration, require change approvals, and routinely test alerting to ensure rapid detection.

oraclecloud.events_rule_identity_provide.title: Event rule for identity provider changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_identity_provide.description: **OCI Events rules** monitor **IAM identity provider** creation, update, and deletion and include a **notification action**. The evaluation identifies rules that filter these events and route matching activity to a notification destination.
oraclecloud.events_rule_identity_provide.risk: Without alerts on **identity provider** changes, federation can be modified unnoticed, enabling unauthorized SSO, privilege escalation, or account takeover. Delayed visibility degrades incident response and threatens **confidentiality** and **integrity** of tenant access.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create rule
2. Set Name and select the target Compartment
3. In Rule condition, add event types: CreateIdentityProvider, DeleteIdentityProvider, UpdateIdentityProvider (service: Identity)
4. In Actions, add Notification, select your Topic
5. Ensure Enabled is On and click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Configure rules to capture **identity provider** `create`, `update`, and `delete` events and send notifications to responders and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on IdP management, require approvals for changes, and test alert paths. Use **defense in depth** with audit logging to spot anomalous identity changes.

oraclecloud.events_rule_idp_group_mappin.title: Event rule for IdP group mapping changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_idp_group_mappin.description: **OCI Events rules** monitor **IdP group mapping changes** with **notification actions** for `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping`, `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.removeidpgroupmapping`, and `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidpgroupmapping`.
oraclecloud.events_rule_idp_group_mappin.risk: Without **alerts** on IdP group mapping changes, federated users can gain unauthorized group memberships unnoticed, enabling **privilege escalation** and broader access to OCI resources. This undermines **confidentiality** and **integrity**, and may affect **availability** through misuse of elevated permissions.

remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Condition: add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.removeidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidpgroupmapping
4. Actions: Add action > Notifications (ONS) and select the target Topic
5. Ensure Rule is Enabled and click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Define **Events rules** for IdP group mapping changes (`com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping`, `...removeidpgroupmapping`, `...updateidpgroupmapping`) and route notifications to monitored channels via **OCI Notifications**. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**, and integrate alerts with a SIEM for **defense in depth**.

oraclecloud.events_rule_local_user_authe.title: Event rule monitoring local OCI user authentication has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_local_user_authe.description: **OCI Events rules** targeting `com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin` are assessed for configured **notification actions** to monitor local user interactive sign-ins. Rules are compartment-scoped and can cover child compartments.
oraclecloud.events_rule_local_user_authe.risk: Without alerts on local sign-ins, **account takeovers** and **brute-force** attempts can go unnoticed. Attackers with local access can exfiltrate data (confidentiality), change configurations (integrity), and disrupt services (availability), delaying detection and response.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Name and select the target Compartment
4. In Condition, set Event Type to: com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin
5. Add Action: choose Notifications, select the Topic, and ensure it is Enabled
6. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Create an Events rule for `com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin` with **notification actions** delivering real-time alerts to monitored channels or workflows. Integrate with a SIEM, tune filters to reduce noise, and apply **least privilege** and **defense in depth** to limit local account exposure.

oraclecloud.events_rule_network_gateway_.title: Event rule monitoring network gateway changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_network_gateway_.description:
**OCI Events rules** monitor **network gateway** lifecycle and attachment changes (DRG, Internet, NAT, Service, and Local Peering gateways) and include **notification actions** so changes generate alerts.

The evaluation looks for rules filtered to these events and confirms they trigger notifications.
oraclecloud.events_rule_network_gateway_.risk:
Unalerted gateway changes can reroute traffic, expose services, or sever connectivity.

Attackers or misconfigurations may modify routes or attachments to enable data exfiltration, man-in-the-middle, or denial of service, degrading **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability**.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_events_rule" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  display_name   = "<example_resource_name>"

  # Critical: Monitor required network gateway event types
  condition = jsonencode({
    eventType = [
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrg",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrg",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrg",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrgattachment",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrgattachment",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrgattachment",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeinternetgatewaycompartment",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createinternetgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteinternetgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateinternetgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changelocalpeeringgatewaycompartment",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletelocalpeeringgateway.end",
      "com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatelocalpeeringgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.natgateway.changenatgatewaycompartment",
      "com.oraclecloud.natgateway.createnatgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.natgateway.deletenatgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.natgateway.updatenatgateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.attachserviceid",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.changeservicegatewaycompartment",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.createservicegateway",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.deleteservicegateway.end",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.detachserviceid",
      "com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.updateservicegateway"
    ]
  })

  actions {
    actions {
      # Critical: Add notification action so the rule passes the check
      action_type = "ONS"   # Sends to Notifications service (ONS)
      topic_id    = "<example_resource_id>"  # ONS topic OCID
    }
  }
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment
3. Set Display name
4. Under Matching events, add these Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeinternetgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changelocalpeeringgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletelocalpeeringgateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatelocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.changenatgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.createnatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.deletenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.updatenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.attachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.changeservicegatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.createservicegateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.deleteservicegateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.detachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.updateservicegateway
5. Add action: Notification, select the target Notifications (ONS) topic
6. Click Create (ensure the rule is enabled)
remediation.recommendationText:
Define **event rules** that match `create`, `update`, `delete`, `attach`, and `detach` actions for all gateway types and send **notifications** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** on topics, cover all compartments/regions, integrate with SIEM, and use **defense in depth** with network change approvals.

oraclecloud.events_rule_network_security.title: Event rule monitoring network security group changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_network_security.description: **OCI Events rules** targeting **Network Security Group (NSG)** changes are evaluated for **notification actions**. Monitored events: `createnetworksecuritygroup`, `updatenetworksecuritygroup`, `deletenetworksecuritygroup`, and `changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment` under `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork`.
oraclecloud.events_rule_network_security.risk:
Absent notifications for NSG changes enable silent policy drift.
- **Confidentiality**: permissive edits can expose services and drive data exfiltration.
- **Integrity**: attackers can reroute traffic or bypass micro-segmentation.
- **Availability**: deletions/misconfigurations may isolate workloads or widen DDoS exposure.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Display name and Compartment
4. Under Conditions, add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createnetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletenetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatenetworksecuritygroup
5. Under Actions, click Add action > Notifications, select Publish to topic, choose the ONS topic
6. Click Create to save the rule
remediation.recommendationText:
Implement **Events** rules for NSG lifecycle changes with **notification actions** to a monitored topic/SIEM.
- Include `createnetworksecuritygroup`, `updatenetworksecuritygroup`, `deletenetworksecuritygroup`, `changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment`
- Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on NSG and Events admins
- Regularly test and tune alerts

oraclecloud.events_rule_route_table_chan.title: Event rule for route table changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_route_table_chan.description:
**OCI Events rules** for **VCN route tables** monitor lifecycle and compartment changes and include **notification actions**.

The evaluation looks for rules that capture `create`, `update`, `delete`, and `changeCompartment` events for route tables and send notifications.
oraclecloud.events_rule_route_table_chan.risk:
Without notifications on route table changes, **routing tampering** can persist unnoticed:
- Exposure of private subnets to the Internet
- Traffic hijack or blackholing
- Segmentation bypass enabling lateral movement
This threatens **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability**.

remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules.
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment; set a Display name.
3. In Condition, add event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeroutetablecompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateroutetable
4. In Actions, add Notifications (ONS) and select the desired Topic.
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create.
remediation.recommendationText: Create an **Events rule** that captures route table `create`, `update`, `delete`, and `changeCompartment` events and routes them to **notifications** used by on-call and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on route edits, require **change approvals**, and apply **defense in depth** with auditing and automated response.

oraclecloud.events_rule_security_list_ch.title: Event rule monitoring security list changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_security_list_ch.description: **OCI Events rules** for VCN **security lists** monitor lifecycle changes-create, update, delete, and compartment moves-and include **notification actions**. The evaluation looks for rules that filter these events and confirms a configured notification target.
oraclecloud.events_rule_security_list_ch.risk: Without timely alerts on security list changes, **unauthorized rule edits** can expose subnets to the Internet, enabling scans, brute force, and lateral movement (**confidentiality**), permit traffic manipulation (**integrity**), or block ports causing outages (**availability**). Delayed detection widens blast radius.

remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule, set a name and compartment
3. In Condition, set Event Type to include exactly:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changesecuritylistcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletesecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist
4. Click Add action, choose Notifications, select an existing topic
5. Ensure the action is enabled and click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Define **Events** rules for security list create/update/delete and route them to **Notifications** or automated responders. Enforce **least privilege** for network and Events admins, apply **change control** with logging, cover critical compartments/regions, and periodically test alerts for reliability.

oraclecloud.events_rule_user_changes.title: Event rule monitoring user changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_user_changes.description:
**OCI Events rules** targeting **IAM user changes** (e.g., `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser` and related update/delete/state events) are assessed for attached **notification actions**.

The finding indicates which rules listen for these events and whether they are configured to emit alerts.
oraclecloud.events_rule_user_changes.risk: Absent alerts on user lifecycle events, **unauthorized account creation**, **privilege escalation**, or **re-enabling disabled users** may go undetected. This delays containment, enabling persistence and lateral movement that erode **confidentiality** and **integrity**, and introduces audit gaps reducing **accountability**.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create Rule
2. Select the Compartment and enter a Name
3. Under Rule Conditions, set Event Type to include:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateusercapabilities
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuserstate
4. Under Actions, add a Notification action and select the desired Notifications (ONS) Topic
5. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText:
Create and maintain **Events rules** for IAM user lifecycle changes and attach reliable **notification actions** to security-owned channels (SIEM, paging, email, chat).

Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rule management, and use **defense in depth** by correlating alerts with audit logs and automating containment.

oraclecloud.events_rule_vcn_changes.title: Event rule monitoring VCN changes has notification actions configured
oraclecloud.events_rule_vcn_changes.description: **OCI Events rules** exist to capture **VCN lifecycle changes** (`create`, `update`, `delete`) via event types `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn`, `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatevcn`, `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletevcn`, and include **notification actions**.
oraclecloud.events_rule_vcn_changes.risk:
Missing alerts for **VCN changes** reduces visibility of network perimeter modifications.

Attackers or mistakes can silently open Internet access, alter routes for **data exfiltration**, or delete gateways/subnets, harming **confidentiality** and **availability**.

remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and enter a name; set Rule state to Enabled
3. Under Conditions, add Event types: com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletevcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatevcn
4. Under Actions, add Notification and select the target Notifications topic
5. Click Create to save the rule
remediation.recommendationText:
Create and enable **Events rules** for VCN lifecycle changes (**create**, **update**, **delete**) with **notification actions** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** to manage rules and notifications, integrate alerts with incident response, and periodically test to support **defense in depth**.

oraclecloud.filestorage_file_system_encr.title: File Storage file system is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
oraclecloud.filestorage_file_system_encr.description: **OCI File Storage** file systems use **Customer-Managed Keys** (`CMEK`) for encryption when a KMS key is associated, instead of the default Oracle-managed encryption.
oraclecloud.filestorage_file_system_encr.risk: Using provider-managed keys limits control over key lifecycle and access, weakening **confidentiality**. You cannot enforce custom rotation, revoke use, or apply granular key permissions, increasing exposure to insider misuse, legal compulsion, or compromised services. It may hinder **compliance** and complicate incident response.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_file_storage_file_system" "<example_resource_name>" {
  availability_domain = "<AVAILABILITY_DOMAIN>"
  compartment_id      = "<COMPARTMENT_OCID>"
  kms_key_id          = "<KMS_KEY_OCID>"  # Critical: associates a customer-managed KMS key to encrypt the file system
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > File Storage > File Systems and select the target file system
3. In the Encryption section, click Edit (or Change key)
4. Select Customer-managed key, choose the Vault and KMS key
5. Click Save to apply
remediation.recommendationText: Encrypt file systems with **Customer-Managed Keys** in OCI KMS. Apply **least privilege** on key usage, enable periodic rotation, and require dual control for key administration. Monitor key activity with centralized logging. Use **defense in depth** by combining `CMEK` with network isolation and strong access governance.

oraclecloud.identity_iam_admins_cannot_u.title: All IAM policies granting manage/use on groups or users in the tenancy restrict access to the Administrators group
oraclecloud.identity_iam_admins_cannot_u.description:
**OCI IAM policies** granting **manage/use** on **groups or users** in the tenancy are evaluated for a condition that excludes the **Administrators** group, such as `target.group.name != 'Administrators'`.

Policies missing this restriction are identified.
oraclecloud.identity_iam_admins_cannot_u.risk: Ability to modify the **Administrators** group enables **privilege escalation** to full tenancy control. This threatens confidentiality (broad data access), integrity (policy/user changes), and availability (resource deletion). Attackers could add persistence accounts, disable safeguards, and evade oversight.

remediation.cli: oci iam policy update --policy-id <example_resource_id> --statements "[\"Allow group <example_resource_name> to manage groups, users in tenancy where target.group.name != 'Administrators'\"]"
remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_identity_policy" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  description    = "<example_resource_name>"
  statements = [
    # Critical: Protect the Administrators group from modification by this policy
    # Adds a where clause so the policy can't target the Administrators group
    "Allow group <example_resource_name> to manage groups, users in tenancy where target.group.name != 'Administrators'"
  ]
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open any policy that allows a group to manage or use groups/users in the tenancy
3. Click Edit policy and update each affected statement to append exactly:
   where target.group.name != 'Administrators'
4. Save changes
5. Repeat for all such policies
remediation.recommendationText: Apply **least privilege**: avoid tenancy-wide manage/use on groups or users. When delegation is required, include a condition excluding the **Administrators** group (e.g., `target.group.name != 'Administrators'`). Enforce **segregation of duties**, require approvals for group changes, and monitor/audit identity policy activity.

oraclecloud.identity_instance_principal_.title: Instance principal authentication is configured for OCI instances, OCI Cloud Databases, and OCI Functions
oraclecloud.identity_instance_principal_.description: **OCI dynamic groups** configured for **instance principal** access to workloads like **Compute instances**, **Functions**, and **Autonomous Databases**. The evaluation looks for matching rules that target these resources (e.g., `instance`, `fnfunc`, `autonomousdatabase`) to confirm workload identity usage.
oraclecloud.identity_instance_principal_.risk: Using user credentials or long-lived keys instead of **instance principals** exposes secrets and weakens **least privilege** and **accountability**. Stolen keys from code or pipelines enable unauthorized API calls, data exfiltration, and privilege abuse, impacting **confidentiality** and **integrity** of OCI resources.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_identity_dynamic_group" "dg" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  description    = "Enable instance principals"
  matching_rule  = "ALL {resource.type = 'instance'}" # Critical: creates a Dynamic Group for instances to enable instance principal auth
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Dynamic Groups
2. Click Create Dynamic Group
3. Enter Name: <example_resource_name>
4. Set Matching Rule to: ALL {resource.type = 'instance'}
5. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText: Adopt **workload identities** with **instance principals** and granular dynamic groups. Apply **least privilege** policies to those groups, avoid long-lived user keys, and remove embedded credentials from code and CI/CD. Monitor access patterns and favor short-lived, auditable tokens as part of a **zero trust** approach.

oraclecloud.identity_no_resources_in_roo.title: No resources exist in the root compartment
oraclecloud.identity_no_resources_in_roo.description: **OCI root compartment** is evaluated for the presence of **user resources**. The finding highlights any assets created at the tenancy root and provides a count per `resource_type`.
oraclecloud.identity_no_resources_in_roo.risk: **Resources in the root compartment** inherit broad tenancy-level policies, weakening **least privilege**. Compromise or error can enable wide **unauthorized access**, **lateral movement**, and destructive changes, degrading **confidentiality** and **integrity**, while complicating audits and quota governance.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
# Place resources in a non-root compartment to avoid creating them in the root
resource "oci_core_vcn" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_compartment_id>" # CRITICAL: ensure this is a non-root compartment OCID to pass the check
  cidr_block     = "10.0.0.0/16"
  display_name   = "<example_resource_name>"
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Governance & Administration > Tenancy Explorer
2. Set Compartment to the root compartment and enable "Show resources in subcompartments" off
3. Note each resource listed in the root compartment
4. For each resource: navigate to its service page (e.g., Compute > Instances), select the resource, click Actions (three dots) > Move resource
5. Choose a non-root compartment and confirm
6. If a resource type cannot be moved, delete it and recreate it in a non-root compartment
7. Repeat until Tenancy Explorer shows 0 resources in the root compartment
remediation.recommendationText:
Reserve the **root compartment** for governance only.
- Create workload-specific child compartments
- Scope IAM to them per **least privilege** and **separation of duties**
- Enforce boundaries with quotas and tags
- Update automation to avoid root placement
- Regularly audit and relocate stray resources

oraclecloud.identity_non_root_compartmen.title: Tenancy has at least one active non-root compartment
oraclecloud.identity_non_root_compartmen.description: **OCI tenancy** includes at least one **active non-root compartment**. Only compartments below the `root` level are considered, indicating that resources are organized outside the root scope.
oraclecloud.identity_non_root_compartmen.risk: Using only the `root` compartment removes segmentation and forces broad tenancy-wide access. This endangers **confidentiality** and **integrity** through cross-project visibility, mis-scoped policies, and accidental changes with global impact, and can affect **availability** via bulk deletions or misconfigurations.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
# Creates a non-root compartment under the tenancy to pass the check
resource "oci_identity_compartment" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>" # Critical: parent OCID (tenancy) for non-root compartment
  name           = "<example_resource_name>" # Critical: compartment name
  description    = "compartment"             # Critical: required to create
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Compartments
2. Click Create Compartment
3. Enter Name: <example_resource_name> and a Description
4. Ensure the Parent Compartment is the tenancy (root) or desired non-root parent
5. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText:
Create dedicated **non-root compartments** per workload, environment, or team; avoid placing resources in the `root` compartment.

Apply granular policies at the compartment level to enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties**. Use a clear hierarchy and tags, and review the design regularly as the tenancy evolves.

oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_exp.title: Identity Domain password policy expires passwords within 365 days
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_exp.description:
**OCI Identity Domain password policies** are evaluated to confirm **password expiration** is configured and set to `<= 365` days (`password_expires_after`). System-managed immutable policies (`SimplePasswordPolicy`, `StandardPasswordPolicy`) are excluded.

*Legacy IAM lacks password expiration; tenancies without Identity Domains require manual assessment.*
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_exp.risk: Missing or >`365`-day **password expiration** extends the window for **credential stuffing**, **brute force**, and use of leaked passwords. This enables unauthorized access, data exposure, and configuration changes, harming **confidentiality** and **integrity**, and allowing attacker persistence after staff turnover.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_identity_domains_password_policy" "<example_resource_name>" {
  idcs_endpoint = "<example_resource_id>"
  name          = "<example_resource_name>"
  schemas       = ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:oracle:idcs:PasswordPolicy"]

  password_expires_after = 365 # Critical: ensures passwords expire within 365 days to pass the check
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select your identity domain
3. In the domain, open Security (or Domain settings) > Password policies
4. Edit the relevant password policy
5. Set "Password expires after (days)" to 365 or less
6. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Enforce **password rotation** at `<= 365` days in Identity Domains. Combine with **MFA**, strong composition rules, history, and minimum password age to prevent reuse. Apply **least privilege**, disable dormant accounts, and regularly review credential policies. *If on legacy IAM, adopt Identity Domains to gain expiration controls.*

oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_min.title: IAM password policy requires passwords to be at least 14 characters long
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_min.description: **OCI IAM password policies** are evaluated to confirm a **minimum password length** of `>= 14` characters is enforced. The assessment considers policies defined in **Identity Domains** and the legacy tenancy policy, and also detects when no password policy exists. System-managed immutable policies (`SimplePasswordPolicy`, `StandardPasswordPolicy`) are excluded.
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_min.risk: Short or missing password requirements weaken authentication, enabling **brute-force**, **password spraying**, and faster **offline cracking**. Compromised accounts can enable unauthorized console/API use, leading to **data exfiltration** (C), **unauthorized changes** (I), and service disruption via destructive actions (A).

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Domains
2. Select <identity_domain_name> > Security > Password policy
3. Set Minimum length to 14 and click Save
4. If you do not use Identity Domains: go to Identity & Security > Authentication settings, edit Password policy, set Minimum password length to 14, and Save
remediation.recommendationText: Enforce a **minimum password length** of `>= 14`, preferably using passphrases. Combine with **MFA**, complexity and reuse limits, lockout/throttling, and routine policy reviews. Apply **least privilege** to limit blast radius and monitor authentication events. *If using external IdPs, require equivalent policies there.*

oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_pre.title: Identity Domain password policy prevents password reuse by remembering at least 24 previous passwords
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_pre.description: **OCI Identity Domains** password policies are evaluated for **password reuse prevention** via **password history** (`num_passwords_in_history >= 24`). System-managed policies (`SimplePasswordPolicy`, `StandardPasswordPolicy`) are excluded. *Legacy IAM lacks password history.*
oraclecloud.identity_password_policy_pre.risk: Without **password history**, users can reuse old passwords. Compromised credentials remain valid after resets, enabling account takeover, unauthorized changes, and **lateral movement**, degrading **confidentiality** and **integrity** and weakening recovery from password-related incidents.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select <identity_domain_name>
3. Open Security > Password policies
4. Edit the affected policy (e.g., Default Password Policy)
5. Set "Number of passwords in history" (Remember previous passwords) to 24
6. Click Save
7. Repeat for any other password policies in the domain
remediation.recommendationText: Enforce **password history** in Identity Domains with `num_passwords_in_history >= 24`. Pair with `min_password_age` to prevent rapid cycling, and maintain strong complexity and expiration rules. *If using legacy IAM, migrate to Identity Domains.* Complement with **MFA** for defense in depth.

oraclecloud.identity_service_level_admin.title: Identity policy does not grant broad 'manage all-resources' permissions
oraclecloud.identity_service_level_admin.description: **OCI IAM policies** are reviewed for **overly broad entitlements**, specifically statements granting `manage all-resources` without scoping to particular services or compartments. Only **active policies** are considered; the default tenant admin policy is excluded.
oraclecloud.identity_service_level_admin.risk: Broad `manage all-resources` grants erode **least privilege**, enabling access across the tenancy. A compromised user or misused token could cause **privilege escalation**, **data exfiltration**, destructive changes, and service disruption, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

remediation.cli: oci iam policy update --policy-id <policy-ocid> --statements '["Allow group <GroupName> to manage instance-family in compartment <CompartmentName>"]'
remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_identity_policy" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  description    = "<policy-description>"

  # Critical: restrict to a specific service family to avoid broad 'manage all-resources'
  statements = [
    "Allow group <GroupName> to manage instance-family in compartment <CompartmentName>"
  ]
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open the policy that contains a statement with "manage all-resources"
3. Click Edit policy statements
4. Remove the statement(s) containing "manage all-resources"
5. Add a service-specific statement, e.g.: Allow group <GroupName> to manage instance-family in compartment <CompartmentName>
6. Click Save changes
remediation.recommendationText:
Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**:
- Replace `manage all-resources` with service-scoped permissions and compartment limits
- Create service-level admin groups for specific families
- Use tags/regions for conditions, *when applicable*
- Employ time-bound elevation and periodic reviews

oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_permi.title: OCI IAM policy does not grant 'manage all-resources in tenancy' unless it is the Tenant Admin Policy
oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_permi.description: **OCI IAM policies** are analyzed for statements granting `manage all-resources in tenancy` to groups. Only the `Tenant Admin Policy` for the Administrators group should include this broad verb. Any other active policy containing this tenancy-wide permission is identified.
oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_permi.risk: Tenancy-wide `manage` rights for non-admins allow complete control of identities and resources. A compromised account can escalate privileges, exfiltrate data across compartments, alter or delete workloads and backups, and disable monitoring-impacting **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability** of the entire tenancy.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_identity_policy" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name           = "<POLICY_NAME>"
  compartment_id = "<example_compartment_id>"
  description    = "Replace tenancy-wide admin with scoped permissions"

  statements = [
    # FIX: Replace "in tenancy" with compartment scope to remove overly broad permission
    "allow group <group_name> to manage all-resources in compartment <compartment_name>"
  ]
}
```
remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open each ACTIVE policy that is NOT named "Tenant Admin Policy"
3. Click Edit policy
4. Remove any statement containing: to manage all-resources in tenancy; or change it to: in compartment <compartment_name>
5. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Restrict `manage all-resources in tenancy` to the **Administrators** group only. Apply **least privilege** by scoping access to compartments and specific resource families, using conditions to narrow rights. Enforce **separation of duties**, maintain a *break-glass* admin model, and review policies regularly to prevent privilege drift.

oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_users.title: Tenancy administrator user has no API keys
oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_users.description: **OCI tenancy administrator accounts** (members of the `Administrators` group) are inspected for configured user **API keys** tied to those identities.
oraclecloud.identity_tenancy_admin_users.risk: **Admin API keys** are long-lived secrets that can be stolen from endpoints or repos, enabling non-interactive, MFA-less access. Attackers could run privileged API calls, exfiltrate data, modify policies, or delete resources, impacting **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability**.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Console
2. Open the navigation menu and go to Identity & Security > Domains
3. Select your domain (<example_resource_name>), then click Users
4. Click the tenancy administrator user (<example_resource_name>)
5. Open the API Keys tab
6. For each API key, click Actions > Delete and confirm
7. Repeat until the API Keys list is empty
remediation.recommendationText: Do not issue **API keys** to tenancy administrators. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**: use non-admin service accounts or principals with narrowly scoped rights and short-lived credentials. Require **SSO/MFA** for admin access, and enforce rapid key revocation and rotation for any programmatic identities.

oraclecloud.identity_user_api_keys_rotat.title: User active API key is rotated within 90 days or less
oraclecloud.identity_user_api_keys_rotat.description: **OCI IAM users** with **active API signing keys** older than `90` days are identified. Key age is derived from each key's creation time; only active keys are considered. Users without API keys are recorded.
oraclecloud.identity_user_api_keys_rotat.risk: Long-lived API keys widen exposure. If a key leaks, an attacker can sign OCI API calls without MFA, enabling unauthorized changes (**integrity**), data access (**confidentiality**), and service outages (**availability**). Delayed rotation prolongs dwell time and complicates incident response.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Users, then select the target user
3. Open API Keys and click Add API Key
4. Generate API Key Pair (or Upload/Paste Public Key), then click Add and download/copy the private key
5. For each API key older than 90 days, click the Actions (three dots) next to its fingerprint and select Delete
6. Confirm deletion
remediation.recommendationText:
Enforce **API key rotation** every `90` days.
- Issue a new key, confirm workloads use it, then revoke the old key
- Apply **least privilege** and avoid shared keys
- Limit active keys per user and remove unused ones
- Monitor usage and automate rotation for **defense in depth**

oraclecloud.identity_user_auth_tokens_ro.title: User auth token age is 90 days or less
oraclecloud.identity_user_auth_tokens_ro.description: **OCI IAM user auth tokens** are evaluated for **rotation age** against a `90-day` threshold using each token's creation time. Tokens older than this window indicate the token has not been recently rotated.
oraclecloud.identity_user_auth_tokens_ro.risk: Stale **auth tokens** increase exposure of **confidential data** and enable **persistent unauthorized API access** if compromised. Long-lived tokens can outlast password resets and role changes, weakening **least privilege** and enabling **lateral movement** and data exfiltration.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Users
2. Open the user with the failing auth token
3. In the Auth Tokens tab, find tokens older than 90 days (check Created date)
4. Select the old token and click Delete
5. Confirm deletion
6. Repeat for any other tokens older than 90 days
remediation.recommendationText: Enforce routine **token rotation** at `<= 90 days` and prefer **short-lived, scoped credentials**. Apply **least privilege**, revoke unused tokens, set **automatic expirations**, and monitor usage. *When possible*, replace static tokens with federated or session-based access to reduce exposure.

oraclecloud.identity_user_customer_secre.title: User customer secret key is rotated within 90 days or less
oraclecloud.identity_user_customer_secre.description: **OCI IAM customer secret keys** are assessed by creation timestamp to determine whether their age exceeds `90` days.
oraclecloud.identity_user_customer_secre.risk:
Long-lived **customer secret keys** keep compromised or brute-forced credentials valid.
Attackers can use them to list, read, write, or delete Object Storage data, enabling exfiltration, tampering, and disruption-impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains > <example_resource_name> > Users > select <example_resource_name>
3. Open the Customer secret keys tab and click Generate secret key; save the Access Key and Secret
4. Delete any key older than 90 days: select the old key and click Delete
remediation.recommendationText: Rotate **customer secret keys** every `<= 90` days. Apply **least privilege**, remove unused keys, and prefer short-lived identities (instance/resource principals) over static secrets. Automate rotation and alerts, avoid embedding keys in code, and continuously monitor key usage.

oraclecloud.identity_user_db_passwords_r.title: User IAM database password was created within the last 90 days
oraclecloud.identity_user_db_passwords_r.description:
**OCI IAM user database passwords** are evaluated for **age**. Passwords are compared to a rotation window of `90 days`, flagging credentials that have not been refreshed within that period for the associated user accounts and regions.

*Covers each user's active database passwords tracked by IAM.*
oraclecloud.identity_user_db_passwords_r.risk: Stale **database credentials** increase exposure to **brute-force**, **credential stuffing**, and reuse of leaked passwords. If compromised, attackers can gain direct DB access, enabling **data exfiltration** (C), unauthorized changes to schemas or data (I), and service disruption via destructive queries (A). Long-lived secrets can bypass offboarding.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select your domain
3. Click Users and open the target user
4. In the user's page, open DB passwords (Database passwords)
5. Click Create DB password (or Reset) and confirm
6. Copy the generated password and update any services using it
remediation.recommendationText:
Enforce rotation of **IAM database passwords** at or below `90 days` and expire old credentials. Automate issuance and revocation, and remove unused DB passwords.

Prefer **short-lived auth** (tokens or certificates) where supported, apply **least privilege** to DB roles, and monitor credential age to prevent drift.

oraclecloud.identity_user_mfa_enabled_co.title: User with console password has MFA enabled for console access
oraclecloud.identity_user_mfa_enabled_co.description: **OCI IAM users** with **console password access** are expected to have **multifactor authentication** enabled. The evaluation inspects each local user allowed to sign in to the Console and identifies those without an active second factor.
oraclecloud.identity_user_mfa_enabled_co.risk:
Console-password accounts without **MFA** are exposed to **phishing**, **credential stuffing**, and **brute force**.

A stolen password can grant Console access, enabling privilege escalation, key creation, and data access-compromising **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability** across OCI.

remediation.other:
1. Enable MFA (user action):
   - Sign in to the OCI Console as the affected user
   - Click your profile icon > User settings
   - Click "Enable Multi-Factor Authentication"
   - Scan the QR code with an authenticator app and enter the verification code, then click "Enable"
2. Or, remove console access (admin action) if the user doesn't need it:
   - In the Console, go to Identity & Security > Users
   - Open the user's page > Edit user capabilities
   - Uncheck "Can use Console password" and Save
remediation.recommendationText: Require **MFA** for all users with Console passwords; prefer **phishing-resistant authenticators** (e.g., FIDO). Enforce via sign-on policies, prioritizing admins. Apply **least privilege**, disable Console passwords for service or federated users, and monitor auth logs to confirm ongoing MFA coverage.

oraclecloud.identity_user_valid_email_ad.title: IAM user has a valid email address
oraclecloud.identity_user_valid_email_ad.description: **OCI IAM user accounts** are evaluated for a populated `email` attribute that resembles an address (contains `@`). Accounts missing this attribute or with malformed values are identified.
oraclecloud.identity_user_valid_email_ad.risk: Missing or invalid emails break **account recovery** and **MFA** flows, silencing security notifications. This degrades **availability** for legitimate users and enables attacker **persistence** on compromised or orphaned accounts, delaying containment and risking unauthorized data access.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
# Ensure the user has a valid email address
resource "oci_identity_user" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  email          = "<example_email@example.com>" # Critical: sets a valid email (contains '@') to pass the check
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Users
3. Select the user without a valid email
4. Click Edit (or Update)
5. Enter a valid email address (must include '@')
6. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Ensure every user has a unique, verified, and monitored `email`. Enforce this at creation and through periodic reviews; disable or remove accounts with invalid addresses. Prefer **federated identities** to minimize local users, and apply **least privilege** with clear ownership to support lifecycle management.

oraclecloud.integration_instance_access_.title: Integration Cloud instance uses a private endpoint or a public endpoint with IP or VCN allowlists
oraclecloud.integration_instance_access_.description: **Oracle Integration Cloud instances** are evaluated for **network endpoint restrictions**, confirming access is limited to approved IPs or VCNs. Configurations with `0.0.0.0/0`, missing endpoint details, or **PUBLIC** endpoints without allowlists are identified; **PRIVATE** endpoints or PUBLIC endpoints with IP/VCN allowlists indicate restricted access.
oraclecloud.integration_instance_access_.risk: Unrestricted OIC endpoints expose integration APIs and consoles to the Internet, enabling credential brute force, token theft, and unauthorized invocations. Attackers can exfiltrate data, alter workflows, and pivot into connected backends, impacting confidentiality and integrity, and causing availability issues via abuse or DoS.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Developer Services > Integration > Integration instances
2. Open <example_resource_name> and click Edit
3. If using Public endpoint: add an entry under Allowed IPs (e.g., <ALLOWED_CIDR>) and remove any 0.0.0.0/0
4. Alternatively, switch to Private endpoint if desired and select the required VCN/subnet
5. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Prefer **PRIVATE** endpoints and restrict access to specific VCNs. *If PUBLIC is required*, enforce strict IP allowlists-never `0.0.0.0/0`. Apply **least privilege** at network layers, place OIC behind **WAF/VPN**, segment with security lists, and monitor access logs. Review allowlists regularly as part of **defense in depth**.

oraclecloud.kms_key_rotation_enabled.title: Customer-managed KMS key has rotation enabled with interval of 365 days or less
oraclecloud.kms_key_rotation_enabled.description: **OCI KMS customer-managed keys** configured for **automatic rotation**, with a rotation interval set to `<= 365` days, or **manually rotated** within the last 365 days. Some vault types do not support auto-rotation, so manual rotation is accepted as an alternative.
oraclecloud.kms_key_rotation_enabled.risk: Without regular rotation, a compromised key can be used longer to decrypt data at rest and backups or to forge signatures. This erodes **confidentiality** and **integrity**, increases the blast radius, and complicates incident response due to broad reuse of the same key version.

remediation.cli: oci kms management key update --key-id <example_resource_id> --endpoint <example_management_endpoint> --is-auto-rotation-enabled true --auto-key-rotation-details '{"rotationIntervalInDays": 365}'
remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Vault
2. Open the vault, then under Resources select Master Encryption Keys
3. Click the target key name
4. For vaults that support auto-rotation: Click Edit auto-rotation settings, enable Auto rotation, set Rotation interval to 365 days (or less), and click Update
5. For vaults that do not support auto-rotation (e.g., External or Virtual Private vaults): Click 'Rotate Key' to manually rotate the key version at least once every 365 days
remediation.recommendationText: Enable **automatic key rotation** and set an interval `<= 365` days (*shorter for sensitive data*). For vault types that do not support auto-rotation (e.g., External or Virtual Private vaults), **manually rotate** the key at least once every 365 days. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties** for key administration. Monitor rotation status, retire old key versions, and ensure applications handle key versioning to prevent outages.

oraclecloud.network_default_security_lis.title: Default security list restricts all traffic except ICMP within VCN
oraclecloud.network_default_security_lis.description: **OCI default security list** of each VCN is evaluated to allow only VCN-internal `ICMP`. Non-`ICMP` ingress from `0.0.0.0/0` or sources outside the VCN, and non-`ICMP` egress to `0.0.0.0/0`, are considered overly permissive. Only default lists are in scope.
oraclecloud.network_default_security_lis.risk: Over-permissive default rules expose subnet workloads to the Internet and enable unrestricted outbound traffic. This risks confidentiality (unauthorized access, data exfiltration), integrity (remote exploitation, lateral movement), and availability (DoS/C2) through broad non-`ICMP` `0.0.0.0/0` paths.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and select your VCN
3. Open Security Lists and select the default security list
4. Click Edit All Rules
5. Remove all non-ICMP ingress and egress rules
6. Add an ingress rule: Protocol ICMP, Source <VCN_CIDR>
7. Add an egress rule: Protocol ICMP, Destination <VCN_CIDR>
8. Save changes
remediation.recommendationText: Adopt a **deny-by-default** stance on the default list: allow only VCN-local `ICMP` for diagnostics. Use dedicated security lists or **network security groups** per application to explicitly allow needed ports and sources, and restrict egress to approved ranges. Review regularly under **least privilege**.

oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.title: Network security group restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389 (RDP)
oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.description: **OCI Network Security Groups** are evaluated for inbound source `0.0.0.0/0` permitting **RDP** on `TCP 3389`, including broad rules (all TCP or any protocol) that implicitly include that port.
oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.risk: Exposed **RDP** enables Internet-scale **brute-force** and **protocol exploit** attempts. Compromise yields interactive access for **data exfiltration** (C), **unauthorized changes** (I), and **service disruption** via ransomware (A), with potential **lateral movement** across the VCN.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Network Security Groups
2. Open the <NSG_NAME>
3. Click Security Rules, then the Ingress tab
4. Find the rule with Source 0.0.0.0/0 and Protocol TCP (or All) allowing port 3389
5. Click Delete to remove the rule
   - If RDP is required, Edit instead and set Source to a specific CIDR (not 0.0.0.0/0)
6. Save changes
remediation.recommendationText: Eliminate open `0.0.0.0/0` rules. Restrict **RDP** to trusted IPs and only when necessary. Prefer **private connectivity** via **VPN**, **bastion/jump hosts**, or **zero-trust** brokers. Apply **least privilege** and time-bound access, monitor logs, and disable RDP where unnecessary.

oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.title: Network security group restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.description: Network security groups with **ingress** from `0.0.0.0/0` exposing **SSH** are identified. This includes rules that explicitly permit `TCP` `22`, use `all` protocols, or define TCP port ranges that encompass `22`.
oraclecloud.network_security_group_ingre.risk: Public **SSH** access enables Internet-wide probing, **brute force**, and **credential stuffing** that can grant shell access. Compromise allows **lateral movement**, data exfiltration (confidentiality), unauthorized changes or malware (integrity), and service disruption or ransomware-driven lockouts (availability).

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Network Security Groups
2. Open the target NSG and go to the Rules tab
3. Find the INGRESS rule with Source 0.0.0.0/0 that includes TCP port 22
4. Click Remove to delete that rule
5. (If SSH is required) Add a new INGRESS rule for TCP port 22 with Source set to a specific trusted CIDR (not 0.0.0.0/0), then Save
remediation.recommendationText: Enforce **least privilege**: limit SSH in NSG rules to trusted CIDRs or private networks. Prefer **bastion access** (e.g., OCI Bastion) or **VPN/private connectivity** over direct Internet exposure. Use key-based auth, disable `PasswordAuthentication`, log and monitor access, and segment workloads for **defense in depth**.

oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.title: Security list restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389 (RDP)
oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.description: **OCI security lists** are evaluated for rules that permit **inbound RDP** from the Internet: any source `0.0.0.0/0` allowing **TCP 3389**-including rules that allow all TCP ports or all protocols-signals public RDP exposure.
oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.risk:
Exposed RDP enables:
- **Brute-force/credential stuffing** to gain console access
- **RCE via RDP flaws** and **lateral movement**

Impact: data exfiltration (confidentiality), unauthorized changes (integrity), and disruption or ransomware (availability).

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and select your VCN
2. Under Resources, click Security Lists and open the list attached to the affected subnet
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 that allows TCP port 3389 or All Protocols
4. Delete that rule, or edit it so Source CIDR is a restricted range (e.g., your IP) and Destination Port is 3389 only
5. Click Save Changes
remediation.recommendationText:
Block Internet access to RDP. 
- Deny `0.0.0.0/0` to `3389`; allow only trusted CIDRs.
- Prefer **private access** via a bastion, VPN, or zero-trust remote management.
- Enforce **least privilege** network rules, use **defense in depth**, and adopt *just-in-time* administrative access.

oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.title: Security list restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.description: **OCI security lists** are evaluated for rules that permit **inbound SSH** from `0.0.0.0/0`. Any rule where the destination includes `TCP 22`-or broader rules allowing all TCP or all protocols from `0.0.0.0/0`-indicates public SSH exposure.
oraclecloud.network_security_list_ingres.risk: **Public SSH access** enables Internet-wide **brute force** and **credential stuffing**, risking unauthorized shell access. Compromise can cause data exfiltration (**confidentiality**), command tampering (**integrity**), service disruption (**availability**), and lateral movement in the VCN.

remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and open your VCN
2. Click Security Lists, then select <example_resource_name>
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 and Protocol TCP (or All) that includes port 22
4. Edit the rule: change Source CIDR to a specific allowed range (e.g., your office IP/CIDR) and set Destination Port Range to 22, or delete the rule
5. Click Save changes
remediation.recommendationText: Restrict **SSH** to trusted sources using least-privilege network rules; avoid `0.0.0.0/0`. Prefer **private access** via VPN/peering or a hardened **bastion**. Apply **network segmentation** (NSGs/security lists) to narrow scope. Enforce **key-based authentication**, disable password login, and monitor access.

oraclecloud.network_vcn_subnet_flow_logs.title: Subnet has VCN flow logging enabled
oraclecloud.network_vcn_subnet_flow_logs.description: **OCI subnets** in a VCN have **network flow logging** configured. Evaluation considers an active `flowlogs` configuration targeting the `VCN` or the specific `subnet` in the same region and associated with a log group.
oraclecloud.network_vcn_subnet_flow_logs.risk: Without flow logs, east-west and ingress/egress traffic is opaque, weakening detection and forensics. Scans, data exfiltration, and lateral movement can go unnoticed, undermining confidentiality and integrity, and delaying response to availability threats like DDoS.

remediation.other:
1. In OCI Console, go to Networking > Flow logs
2. Click Enable flow logs
3. Select a Log group (or create one) and a Capture filter (or create one)
4. Click Next, then Add enablement points
5. Choose Virtual cloud network and select your VCN (or choose Subnet and select the subnet)
6. Click Add enablement points, then Next, then Enable flow logs
remediation.recommendationText: Enable **VCN flow logs** for all subnets-prefer VCN-wide enablement for complete coverage-and route to centralized log groups. Enforce least privilege on log access, set retention, and integrate with a SIEM. Use `capture filters` and `sampling` to control volume. Review logs to support defense-in-depth.

oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_encrypt.title: Object Storage bucket is encrypted with a Customer Managed Key (CMK)
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_encrypt.description: **OCI Object Storage buckets** use **customer-managed encryption keys** (`CMEK`) for server-side encryption, with an associated KMS key configured on the bucket.
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_encrypt.risk: Without `CMEK`, encryption relies on provider-managed keys, reducing control over **confidentiality** and key lifecycle. You cannot strictly limit key usage, enforce custom rotation, or revoke keys for crypto-erasure, increasing exposure to unauthorized decryption, data exfiltration, and auditability gaps.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_objectstorage_bucket" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  namespace      = "<example_resource_name>"

  kms_key_id = "<example_resource_id>" # Critical: sets the Customer Managed Key to encrypt the bucket
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Object Storage & Archive Storage > Buckets
3. Open the target bucket
4. Click Edit bucket
5. Under Encryption, select Customer-managed key and choose the desired Vault key
6. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Encrypt buckets with `CMEK`. Apply **least privilege** to key usage, enforce **separation of duties** between key and storage admins, mandate regular rotation, and monitor key access. Use **defense in depth** so encryption complements strict IAM and network controls rather than replacing them.

oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_logging.title: Object Storage bucket has write-level logging enabled
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_logging.description:
**OCI Object Storage buckets** have service logs for **write access events** enabled.

The evaluation identifies buckets with an active `write` logging category scoped to the bucket and region; only `read` logging does not satisfy this condition.
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_logging.risk:
Without **write logging**, unauthorized or accidental overwrites and deletions can go **undetected**, degrading **data integrity** and **availability**.

Missing audit evidence weakens **non-repudiation**, impedes incident response, and allows covert tampering without reliable forensic reconstruction.

remediation.cli: oci logging log create --log-group-id <log-group-ocid> --display-name ObjectStorage-Write-Logs --log-type SERVICE --configuration '{"compartmentId":"<compartment-ocid>","source":{"service":"objectstorage","resource":"<bucket-name>","category":"write","sourceType":"OCISERVICE"}}'
remediation.other:
1. In the OCI Console, select the target region and go to Observability & Management > Logging > Log groups
2. Open an existing log group or click Create log group
3. Click Create log
4. Type: Service
5. Service: Object Storage
6. Category: write
7. Resource: select the target bucket (bucket name must match)
8. Ensure Enabled is checked
9. Click Create
remediation.recommendationText:
Enable `write` service logs on all buckets and route them to a centralized log group for monitoring.

Apply **least privilege** to log data, enforce retention and immutability, and alert on anomalous write activity. Use **defense in depth** so bucket changes are accountable and swiftly detected.

oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_not_pub.title: Object Storage bucket is not publicly accessible
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_not_pub.description: **OCI Object Storage buckets** are assessed for **public accessibility**. Buckets configured as `NoPublicAccess` deny anonymous reads; any other public access setting indicates bucket contents may be reachable without authentication.
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_not_pub.risk: **Public buckets** enable unauthenticated downloads and content listing, compromising **confidentiality** and exposing metadata. Hotlinking can drive unexpected **egress costs** and degrade **availability** through bandwidth exhaustion and service abuse.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_objectstorage_bucket" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id     = "<example_resource_id>"
  name               = "<example_resource_name>"
  namespace          = "<example_namespace_name>"
  public_access_type = "NoPublicAccess" # Critical: makes the bucket private
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Object Storage > Buckets and open <bucket-name>
3. Click Edit (Bucket details)
4. Set Public access type to "No public access"
5. Click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Keep buckets **private** (`NoPublicAccess`) under the **least privilege** principle. For external sharing, use **pre-authenticated requests** or signed URLs with scoped permissions and expiry. Restrict access via IAM policies, enforce guardrails (*e.g.*, Security Zones), and regularly review bucket visibility.

oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_version.title: Object Storage bucket has versioning enabled
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_version.description: **OCI Object Storage buckets** are assessed for **versioning** being set to `Enabled`, indicating prior object versions are retained when updates or deletions occur.
oraclecloud.objectstorage_bucket_version.risk: **No versioning** lets overwrites or deletions permanently remove data, harming **availability** and **integrity**. Malicious or accidental actions, automated jobs, or malware can wipe or corrupt objects without rollback, enabling **ransomware-style** encryption and large-scale data loss.

remediation.terraform:
```hcl
resource "oci_objectstorage_bucket" "<example_resource_name>" {
  compartment_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name           = "<example_resource_name>"
  namespace      = "<example_resource_id>"
  versioning     = "Enabled" # Critical: enables bucket versioning to pass the check
}
```
remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Buckets and open the target bucket
3. In Bucket details, find Versioning and click Edit
4. Select Enabled and click Save
remediation.recommendationText: Enable **bucket versioning** (`Enabled`) for data that needs recovery. Apply **least privilege** to delete and overwrite actions, use **retention rules** or legal holds for critical data, and add **lifecycle policies** to manage older versions-providing **defense in depth** against destructive changes.

scaleway.iam_api_keys_no_root_owned.title: Scaleway IAM API keys must not be owned by the account root user
scaleway.iam_api_keys_no_root_owned.description: **Scaleway API keys** are checked to ensure none is bound to the **account root user**. The account root user is the original Scaleway account owner; its credentials bypass IAM policies and grant unrestricted access to the entire organization.
scaleway.iam_api_keys_no_root_owned.risk: API keys owned by the **account root user** cannot be scoped down with IAM policies. Leaking one of these keys yields immediate full control over every project, resource and billing setting in the organization, and rotating them disrupts every automation depending on root credentials.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Scaleway console as a user with IAM admin permissions.
2. Create a dedicated IAM user or application scoped with the minimum required policy.
3. Generate a new API key for that bearer and roll it out to the workloads currently using the root key.
4. Delete the API key owned by the account root user from the IAM > API keys page.
remediation.recommendationText: Never use API keys owned by the **account root user** for automation. Create scoped **IAM users** or **applications**, attach **least-privilege policies**, and rotate any existing root API keys to that new bearer.

vercel.authentication_no_stale_tokens.title: Vercel API tokens are not stale or unused for over 90 days
vercel.authentication_no_stale_tokens.description: **Vercel API tokens** are assessed for **staleness** by checking whether each token has been active within the last 90 days. Stale tokens that remain unused for extended periods represent unnecessary access credentials that increase the attack surface. Tokens with no recorded activity are also flagged.
vercel.authentication_no_stale_tokens.risk: Stale tokens that have not been used for over **90 days** may belong to decommissioned integrations, former team members, or forgotten automation. These tokens remain **valid** and could be compromised or misused without detection, as their inactivity makes suspicious usage harder to notice in access logs.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to Account Settings > Tokens
3. Review the last active date for each token
4. Revoke or delete tokens that have not been used in over 90 days
5. Contact token owners to confirm whether the token is still needed
6. Implement a regular token review process (e.g., quarterly)
remediation.recommendationText: Regularly audit API tokens and revoke any that have not been used within 90 days. Implement a token lifecycle management process that includes periodic reviews, automatic expiration dates, and documentation of each token's purpose and owner.

vercel.authentication_no_stale_tokens.notes: The stale threshold is configurable via ``stale_token_threshold_days`` in audit_config (default: 90 days). Tokens with no recorded activity (active_at is None) are considered stale.

vercel.authentication_token_not_expired.title: Vercel API tokens have not expired
vercel.authentication_token_not_expired.description: **Vercel API tokens** are assessed for **expiration status** to identify expired tokens or those about to expire within a configurable threshold (default: 7 days). Tokens about to expire are flagged proactively so they can be rotated before causing disruptions. Tokens without an expiration date are considered valid.
vercel.authentication_token_not_expired.risk: Expired tokens indicate poor **token lifecycle management**. Tokens about to expire risk **imminent service disruption** if not rotated in time. Integrations or **CI/CD pipelines** relying on expired or soon-to-expire tokens will fail silently.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to Account Settings > Tokens
3. Identify any expired tokens
4. Delete expired tokens that are no longer needed
5. Create new tokens with appropriate expiration dates to replace expired ones
6. Update any integrations or CI/CD pipelines that used the expired tokens
remediation.recommendationText: Remove expired tokens and create new ones with appropriate expiration dates. Implement a token rotation schedule to ensure tokens are refreshed before they expire. Update all integrations and automation that depend on the replaced tokens.

vercel.authentication_token_not_expired.notes: Tokens without an expiration date (expires_at is None) are treated as valid since they have no defined expiry. The days_to_expire_threshold is configurable via audit_config (default: 7 days). Tokens expiring within the threshold are reported with medium severity; already expired tokens are reported with high severity.

vercel.deployment_production_uses_stable.title: Vercel production deployments originate from a stable branch
vercel.deployment_production_uses_stable.description: **Vercel production deployments** are assessed for **source branch stability** by verifying they are sourced from a stable branch (`main` or `master`). Deploying to production from feature branches bypasses standard CI/CD review processes and may introduce untested or incomplete code into the production environment.
vercel.deployment_production_uses_stable.risk: Production deployments from **feature branches** may contain untested, incomplete, or unapproved code changes. This bypasses the standard **code review and merge workflow**, increasing the risk of shipping bugs, security vulnerabilities, or breaking changes to end users.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to the project Settings > Git
3. Ensure the Production Branch is set to 'main' or 'master'
4. Review recent production deployments and revert any that originated from feature branches
remediation.recommendationText: Configure the production branch to main or master and ensure all production deployments go through the standard merge workflow. Use branch protection rules in your Git provider to prevent direct pushes to the production branch.

vercel.deployment_production_uses_stable.notes: Deployments without git source information are skipped as they may be manual deployments or CLI-triggered builds.

vercel.domain_dns_properly_configured.title: Vercel domain DNS records are properly configured
vercel.domain_dns_properly_configured.description: **Vercel domains** are assessed for **DNS configuration** to verify records properly point to Vercel's infrastructure. Misconfigured DNS can result in domains that fail to serve content, SSL certificate provisioning failures, and degraded user experience.
vercel.domain_dns_properly_configured.risk: **Misconfigured DNS records** can cause the domain to be unreachable, preventing users from accessing the application. It can also prevent **SSL certificate provisioning**, resulting in browser security warnings. Stale DNS configurations may point to decommissioned infrastructure, creating a risk of **subdomain takeover**.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to the project Settings > Domains
3. Review the DNS configuration status for each domain
4. Update DNS records at your domain registrar to match the values shown in the Vercel dashboard
5. Wait for DNS propagation (typically 24-48 hours)
remediation.recommendationText: Update DNS records at your domain registrar to correctly point to Vercel. Use a CNAME record for subdomains or an A record for apex domains. Verify the configuration in the Vercel dashboard after making changes.

vercel.domain_ssl_certificate_valid.title: Vercel domains have a valid, non-expired SSL certificate
vercel.domain_ssl_certificate_valid.description: **Vercel domains** are assessed for **SSL certificate validity** including provisioning, expiration, and upcoming expiry. Vercel automatically provisions and renews SSL certificates for properly configured domains. A missing, expired, or soon-to-expire certificate indicates a configuration issue that may leave traffic unencrypted.
vercel.domain_ssl_certificate_valid.risk: Without an **SSL certificate**, traffic between users and the domain is transmitted in **plain text**. This exposes sensitive data such as authentication tokens, form submissions, and personal information to interception via **man-in-the-middle attacks**. Search engines also penalize non-HTTPS sites, reducing visibility.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to the project Settings > Domains
3. Verify the domain's DNS records point to Vercel correctly
4. Vercel will automatically provision an SSL certificate once DNS is properly configured
5. If issues persist, remove and re-add the domain
remediation.recommendationText: Ensure domain DNS records are properly configured to point to Vercel. Once DNS is validated, Vercel automatically provisions and renews SSL/TLS certificates. Check the domain configuration in the Vercel dashboard if the certificate is not being issued.

vercel.domain_verified.title: Vercel domains are verified
vercel.domain_verified.description: **Vercel domains** are assessed for **ownership verification** status. Unverified domains may not serve traffic correctly and could indicate a pending or incomplete domain setup. Domain verification confirms that the domain owner has authorized Vercel to manage the domain.
vercel.domain_verified.risk: **Unverified domains** may fail to resolve or serve content, causing **downtime** for users. An unverified domain could also indicate a stale or orphaned configuration, or a domain that was added but never properly transferred, creating potential for **domain takeover** if the ownership verification is left incomplete.

remediation.other:
1. Sign in to the Vercel dashboard
2. Navigate to the project Settings > Domains
3. For any unverified domain, follow the verification steps shown
4. Add the required DNS records (CNAME or A record) at your domain registrar
5. Wait for DNS propagation and verify the domain
remediation.recommendationText: Complete domain verification by configuring the required DNS records at your domain registrar. Remove any domains that are no longer needed to reduce the attack surface. Regularly audit domain configurations to ensure all domains remain verified.

vercel.project_auto_expose_system_env_di.title: Vercel project has automatic exposure of system environment variables disabled
